relationship: A student's set memberships determine the corresponding notation and whether union, intersection or complement rules select that student.

learnerLoop.action: Change student memberships and choose the recipient rule.
learnerLoop.modelChange: Each student's membership representation and selected-recipient preview update.
learnerLoop.evidence: The membership display, live notation and recipient count show the exact set operation.
learnerLoop.nextDecision: Change a membership to test a boundary case or revise the rule before sending.

invariants: Each student's set-membership truth is represented consistently in the diagram, notation and operation results.
Union, intersection and complement select regions according to their set definitions.
safeAdaptations: Vary labels, students and target set operations.
Use alternative visual or interactive representations while keeping membership facts, notation and operation results consistent.
nonGoals: Treating overlapping and exclusive regions as the same membership.

task.description: Current set-membership placement or operation request and case progression.

model.description: Venn regions and movable student cards encode membership by card position.
model.visibility: Present throughout; people and regions update after each move.

working.description: Set-rule choices and physical placement actions for the current case.
working.visibility: Placement requirements or operation choices are generated by case.

evidence.description: Membership trace, live notation, recipient count/set and send feedback show the evaluated rule.
evidence.visibility: Updates after selection, movement and send attempts.

completion.description: Correct placement or sent operation result and case progression.
completion.visibility: Operation completion follows a correct send; placement completion is shown in the board feedback.

controls.description: Region moves, rule choices, send and reset actions.
controls.visibility: Operation send and rule controls are present only for operation cases.

membership.description: Each generated student card's membership in A, B, overlap or outside.
membership.domain: Four-valued region membership for eight people.
membership.source: Card centre coordinates relative to the two circles.

operation-rule.description: A, B, union, intersection, complement and compound predicate choices.
operation-rule.domain: Set expression selected by generated rule controls.

recipient-set.description: People satisfying the current operation predicate, including the recipient count.
recipient-set.domain: Set of generated student IDs and whole-number count.

placement-requirements.description: Required region counts/placements for placement cases.

modes.placement: Placement cases ask the learner to move highlighted student cards into required Venn regions; send is hidden.
modes.operation: Operation cases expose single, binary or complement rule choices and require sending to the resulting recipients.
modes.case-order: The source has six generated cases: place one, place four, union, intersection, not-A and neither; later cases unlock from completed earlier cases.
modes.support: No None/Some/All or separate support setting exists in this source.

dependencies: Only the highlighted/selected student can be moved by a region control; moving a card recomputes membership and clears a prior sent state.
Placement completes when all generated requirements are correct. Operation completion requires a send whose recipient set exactly matches the predicate.
Changing operator or complement choice invalidates the prior send; case tabs remain gated by earlier completion.
Region membership is derived from the card centre, so boundary placement changes the evaluated set.
implementation.completion: The source adds a case to completed after all placement requirements pass or an operation send has the exact target predicate; the next case becomes available through the case tabs/state.
limitations: People and placement/rule controls are generated for the current case; student IDs and per-choice selectors are not fixed across cases.
There is no typed set-notation answer; selection, movement and send are the answer mechanics.
